claims.summary: Observed: scan_known_model_control_markers (L114) rebuilds a non-destructive 'remainder', keeping a marker's bytes only when reference_syntax is Some; report frames this as preserving markers 'when identified as active instructions'.
claims.disposition: verified_existing; contradiction preserved. Source L129-131 pushes the token ONLY when reference_syntax.is_some() (L49-60: quoted/grouped/explicit-relation). The report inverts it: preservation is for REFERENCE contexts; a bare ACTIVE marker with no reference grammar is STRIPPED. Not domesticated. Locked by scan_known_model_control_markers_preserves_grouped_and_explicit_relation_contexts (tests.rs L2845).

claims.summary: Observed: first_word_after (L89-96) yields the first alphanumeric word after the marker; followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation (L64-86) tests it against a finite matches! verb allowlist (appears/as/behaves/.../serves/signals).
claims.disposition: verified_existing. Source L64-96 exactly as described; the allowlist lives in followed_by_explicit_exact_token_relation (not first_word_after, minor attribution slip, line numbers correct). Locked by control_marker_relation_word_scanner_keeps_unicode_alphanumerics_together (L2112) and control_marker_cleanup_uses_only_the_first_finite_relation_word (L2565).

claims.summary: Snag: a verb absent from the matches! block returns false; with no reference delimiters, reference_syntax is None and the marker is dropped from the remainder ('over-sanitization of complex prompts'), 'even if intended as a functional instruction'.
claims.disposition: verified_existing; mechanism is source-accurate (L49-60,64-86,129-131). Correction: stripping an ACTIVELY-used marker is the intended defense; the real over-sanitization risk is a REFERENCED marker with a novel verb. Widening the finite allowlist = Tier-5 live grammar, NOT done. Boundary locked by control_marker_cleanup_distinguishes_allowlisted_is_from_unlisted_acts (L2528: unlisted 'acts' -> removed_total=1).

claims.summary: Test 1 (Functional): verify behavior when a marker is followed by a non-whitelisted but functionally relevant verb (e.g. 'operates') to see if it is identified as a non-directive.
claims.disposition: verified_existing. 'operates' is behaviorally identical to the locked unlisted-verb cases: control_marker_cleanup_distinguishes_allowlisted_is_from_unlisted_acts (L2528) plus does_not_expand_relation_allowlist_to_implies/contains/creates/triggers (L2595-2655). An 'operates' twin would be activity without evidentiary value; the boundary is already a regression.

claims.summary: Test 2 (Boundary): a marker nested in multiple non-standard delimiters (e.g. «[MARKER]») should keep exact_reference_delimiter_syntax (L199) recognizing QuotedExactKnownToken and preserving marker visibility.
claims.disposition: verified_existing; sub-contradiction preserved. «» is a QuotedExactKnownToken pair (L164), [] a Grouped pair (L177); the innermost adjacent pair to the marker ([]) sets context, so «[MARKER]» classifies GroupedExactKnownToken, not Quoted -- but reference_syntax is Some either way, so preservation holds. Locked by preserves_non_ascii_matching_quote_pairs (L2302), preserves_nested_fullwidth_cjk_reference_stack (L2343), preserves_bounded_nested_delimiter_stacks (L2176), reports_double_square_bracket_depth_two (L2876).
